newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng soars over two pct in afternoon.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng soars over two pct in afternoon.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index soared more than two percent in Thursday afternoon trade after the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping removed the uncertainty hanging over the market during recent sessions.
The blue chip index rose to a session high of 13,419.05, up 312.73 points or 2.39 percent compared with Wednesday's close.
Turnover was a buoyant HK$8.26 billion (US$1.06 billion).
China announced Deng died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection.
"This is something that stock markets have been gearing up for for some considerable time," said Peter Churchouse, regional strategist at Morgan Stanley.

"People have got used to the idea and thought long and hard about likely directions in China post-Deng anyway. People have got their own views and have become more or less comfortable with them," he said.

Concerns about Deng Xiaoping's health contributed to a recent slide in Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index. From an all-time high of 14,004.93 on January 16, the blue chip barometer has tumbled 899 points to Wednesday's close of 13,106.32.
"It was seen as getting back into buy territory again," said Pauline Gately, regional strategist at Merrill Lynch.
Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International, said investors were looking forward to a new phase of the market.
"They are probably looking at the 14,000 level with this kind of buying momentum," he said.
Hang Seng Index futures also traded higher on Thursday. The February contract jumped 335 points to 13,415.
"It's nice to have the rumours of Deng's death finally out of the picture," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager Nikko Securities.
Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities, said investors felt that "the last detectable uncertainty in China has been removed with the death of Deng Xiaoping".
"Based on the fundamentals and the economic development in China, there should be further upside potential," he said.
The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong issued a statement saying trading was being conducted as usual.

"The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong regrets to learn of the death of Deng Xiaoping. The Exchange is monitoring the markets closely and has found that our markets have been operating in an orderly and efficient manner," it said.
Among the blue chips, Swire Pacific rose HK$2.00 to HK$66.75 and Cheung Kong advanced HK$1.75 to HK$72.75. HSBC Holdings was up HK$2.50 at HK$187.50. (US$1=HK$7.8)
